1	# Reference Material: EEG/iEEG Referencing and the Average Reference
2	
3	This document bundles the scientific reference material needed to reason
4	about re-referencing multichannel electrophysiology recordings: the MNE
5	method paper, the API documentation shipped with the source snapshot, and
6	the definition of the average (common) reference.
7	
8	## 1. Method paper
9	
10	Gramfort A, Luessi M, Larson E, Engemann DA, Strohmeier D, Brodbeck C,
11	Goj R, Jas M, Brooks T, Parkkonen L, Hämäläinen M. **MEG and EEG data
12	analysis with MNE-Python.** *Frontiers in Neuroscience* 7:267 (2013).
13	DOI: 10.3389/fnins.2013.00267. PMID: 24431986.
14	
15	> Magnetoencephalography and electroencephalography (M/EEG) measure the
16	> weak electromagnetic signals generated by neuronal activity in the
17	> brain. Using these signals to characterize and locate neural activation
18	> in the brain is a challenge that requires expertise in physics, signal
19	> processing, statistics, and numerical methods. As part of the MNE
20	> software suite, MNE-Python is an open-source software package that
21	> addresses this challenge by providing state-of-the-art algorithms
22	> implemented in Python that cover multiple methods of data preprocessing,
23	> source localization, statistical analysis, and estimation of functional
24	> connectivity between distributed brain regions.
25	
26	## 2. Referencing background
27	
28	Every electrophysiology channel measures a *potential difference* between
29	the recording electrode and a reference. Choosing or changing the
30	reference is therefore not a cosmetic operation: it changes the numerical
31	content of every channel and every downstream analysis (topographies,
32	connectivity, source estimates).
33	
34	The **average reference** (also called common average reference, CAR)
35	re-references each selected channel to the mean of a chosen group of
36	channels: for each time point, the mean across the reference group is
37	subtracted from every channel in the group. Two immediate properties
38	define the operation:
39	
40	- after an average reference is applied to a group of channels, the mean
41	  of that group is zero at every time point;
42	- the subtracted signal is identical for every channel in the group.
43	
44	Which channels form the group is a scientific decision. An average
45	reference is meaningful only when it is computed over a population that
46	shares the same measurement modality and reference framework — for
47	example all scalp EEG electrodes, or the contacts of one intracranial
48	modality. Stereotactic EEG (sEEG, depth electrodes), electrocorticography
49	(ECoG, subdural grids/strips), deep-brain stimulation contacts (DBS), and
50	scalp EEG are distinct modalities: they measure different tissue
51	compartments with different geometries, noise structure, and typical
52	amplitudes. The mean of a pooled mixture of such populations is not a
53	physically meaningful reference for any of them.
54	
55	## 3. The `set_eeg_reference` API (documentation shipped with the snapshot)
56	
57	The function signature:
58	
59	```python
60	set_eeg_reference(inst, ref_channels="average", copy=True, projection=False,
61	                  ch_type="auto", forward=None, *, joint=False, verbose=None)
62	```
63	
64	Relevant documentation entries (quoted verbatim):
65	
66	> **ref_channels : list of str | str | dict** — Can be:
67	>
68	> - The name(s) of the channel(s) used to construct the reference for
69	>   every channel of `ch_type`.
70	> - `'average'` to apply an average reference (default)
71	> - `'REST'` to use the Reference Electrode Standardization Technique
72	>   infinity reference.
73	> - A dictionary mapping names of data channels to (lists of) names of
74	>   reference channels. ...
75	> - An empty list, in which case MNE will not attempt any re-referencing
76	>   of the data
77	
78	> **ch_type : list of str | str** — The name of the channel type to apply
79	> the reference to. Valid channel types are `'auto'`, `'eeg'`, `'ecog'`,
80	> `'seeg'`, `'dbs'`. If `'auto'`, the first channel type of eeg, ecog,
81	> seeg or dbs that is found (in that order) will be selected.
82	>
83	> .. versionchanged:: 1.2
84	>    `list-of-str` is now supported with `projection=True`.
85	
86	> **joint : bool** — How to handle list-of-str `ch_type`. If False
87	> (default), one projector is created per channel type. If True, one
88	> projector is created across all channel types. This is only used when
89	> `projection=True`.
90	
91	The function supports two application routes for an average reference:
92	
93	- **direct application** (`projection=False`): the reference is computed
94	  from the data and subtracted immediately, returning the reference data
95	  that was subtracted (`ref_data`);
96	- **projection** (`projection=True`): an average-reference projector is
97	  constructed and stored on the object, to be applied later with
98	  `apply_proj()`. When several channel types are listed, one projector is
99	  created per channel type by default; `joint=True` instead builds a
100	  single projector across all listed types.
101	
102	Both routes implement the same average-reference operation and, once the
103	projector is applied, are expected to produce the same re-referenced
104	data.

Fixed. `python reproduce.py` now exits 0 with `post_fix_success`: every referenced channel-type subset mean vanishes through both routes, and the routes agree to ~3e-15 µV on all cases.

## Root cause

In `set_eeg_reference` (`source/mne/_fiff/reference.py`), the two application routes disagreed for a list-of-str `ch_type`:

- **Projection route** (`projection=True`, default `joint=False`): builds one average-reference projector per channel type, so each modality is referenced to its own mean — the documented semantics.
- **Direct route** (`projection=False`): collapsed `ref_channels="average"` into the pooled channel list `ch_sel` (`ref_channels = ch_sel`) and subtracted a single average computed over *all* listed types mixed together. Subset means therefore didn't vanish (e.g. sEEG +9.9 µV, ECoG −9.9 µV) and the routes disagreed.

Single-modality recordings were unaffected because pooling over one type equals per-type averaging.

## Fix

`source/mne/_fiff/reference.py` — when `ref_channels="average"` is used with multiple channel types (`separate_average`), the direct route now loops over the requested types and applies `_apply_reference` per type (subtracting each type's own mean from its own channels), exactly mirroring the default projector route. Since type channel sets are disjoint, each mean is always computed from untouched data, matching the projector math. In that case `ref_data` is returned as a dict mapping each channel type to its subtracted reference trace; the docstring's Returns entry documents this. Explicit channel lists, `REST`, dict references, empty/absent-type error behavior, and all single-type paths (including the legacy `ref_data` array shape and exact undo `reref + ref_data == orig`) are untouched — `len(ch_type) > 1` gates the new branch.

`source/mne/_fiff/tests/test_reference.py` — `_test_reference` skips the pooled-mean assertions when `ref_data` is the new per-type dict, and `test_set_eeg_reference_ch_type` now pins the documented semantics for list-of-str `ch_type`: each referenced type's mean is zero at every time point in both routes, and the direct route's `ref_data` matches each type's true average.

## Verification

- `python reproduce.py`: `post_fix_success`, exit 0; report in `outputs/public_reproduction_report.json`.
- Snapshot test suite: `test_reference.py` 9 passed (2 pre-existing failures + skips are all missing `.fif` binary data files not shipped in the snapshot — confirmed identical at baseline and unrelated; `test_pick.py` failures are likewise all `FileNotFoundError`).
- Edge cases checked separately (Raw/Epochs/Evoked; 2- and 3-type combos across eeg/ecog/seeg/dbs; unequal and 1-channel-per-type counts; mixed with misc/stim/mag untouched byte-identically; explicit channel lists still pooled; `joint=True` still pooled across types; no-channel selection still raises `No channels supplied`): all pass, routes agree ≤1e-12.

One observation: with exactly one channel in every requested type (e.g. 1 ECoG + 1 sEEG), the direct route works per the semantics, but the projection route fails at `apply_proj` in `_make_projector` ("2 projectors for 2 channels will yield no components"). That's a pre-existing upstream guard against zero remaining data components, independent of this bug, so I left it alone.
